channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: ICB exec pay under review after mergers
item.description: The government is considering steps to stop integrated care board executives receiving pay rises simply because their organisations merge and cover bigger populations.

item.title: Leaders ‘disconnected’ from front line at high-secure hospital
item.description: Bosses at a trust being investigated for corporate manslaughter have been criticised by a regulator, which found care and patient dignity failings, and a “disconnect” between senior leaders and frontline staff at its high-secure hospital.

item.title: Chemo delays blamed on bank pay cuts
item.description: Patients have been waiting up to a month for chemotherapy appointments because of staffing shortages, partly caused by reductions in bank rates.

item.title: Investigation after patient ordered poison to inpatient unit
item.description: The Care Quality Commission is examining the circumstances surrounding the death of a patient at a psychiatric hospital in Birmingham.

item.title: £460m patient transport deal collapses again
item.description: Plans for the supply of non-emergency patient transport services across the North West lie in ruins for the second time within 20 months after two of its three regional lots were abandoned.

item.title: Former chief crown prosecutor to chair biggest trust
item.description: A former chief crown prosecutor has been appointed to chair England’s largest trust.

item.title: Pay rise above 2.4% would hit elective targets, DHSC warns
item.description: A pay award above 2.4 per cent for NHS staff next year could mean a “reduction in ambitions” for cutting waiting lists, the government has warned.

item.title: Virtual ward patient died due to failure to transfer him to hospital
item.description: The death of a man being cared for on a virtual ward was the result of a “catalogue of failings” by two trusts, a coroner has ruled.

item.title: Mental health will always struggle for money but tech offers hope, says national director
item.description: The national director for mental health has admitted the sector will always struggle for adequate funding, but said it was no longer the “poor relative” of the acute sector when it came to digital investment.

item.title: Exclusive: Government maternity review condemned for reliance on AI
item.description: A national review’s poor use of AI to analyse evidence contributed to the downplaying of a key factor in the deaths of mothers and babies, according to one of its leading members.

item.title: Investigation launched after staff access care record of man killed by tiger
item.description: Two NHS staff may have accessed or tried to access medical information about a man killed by a tiger at a wildlife park “without a legitimate reason”, a trust has said.

item.title: ICB’s £600m spend lacks ‘detailed analysis’
item.description: An ICB team responsible for an annual spend of nearly £600m is signing off “high cost” care packages without “detailed analysis” while also undergoing a review into its working culture, the commissioner has revealed.

item.title: No ‘space’ for an IHO here, says trust CEO
item.description: The CEO of one of the NHS’s best-performing trusts has told HSJ he does not think “there’s much space” for an integrated health organisation in his area.

item.title: Government U-turns on transfer of ICB functions
item.description: Integrated care boards will have to carry out more than a dozen functions earmarked for transfer to other bodies for at least another year despite huge cuts in their workforce, HSJ has learned.

item.title: Regional director made chair of struggling hospital group
item.description: A NHS England regional director has been announced as interim chair of a hospital group facing significant financial challenges and leadership instability.

item.title: Trust to top up funding of struggling GP practices
item.description: An acute and community trust has decided to use its own money to boost the funding of a dozen local GP practices with low patient satisfaction scores, HSJ has learned.

item.title: Supplier payments delayed as trust cashflows go ‘critical’
item.description: Some of the NHS’s most financially challenged trusts are paying less than half of their suppliers on time as cash flow becomes “critical”, an HSJ investigation has discovered.

item.title: ‘My mind is blown’: MP reacts to CEO’s admission
item.description: The new leadership of a troubled NHS trust has been accused of losing focus and “struggling” to improve the provider’s performance by one of its local MPs.

item.title: NHSE abolition on the cusp of being delayed
item.description: The abolition of NHS England will have to be formally delayed beyond April 2027 unless decisions about future national structures are made within days, HSJ understands.

item.title: Inquiry trust told to act on rise in inpatient deaths
item.description: Commissioners have demanded an action plan after an “increase of inpatient deaths” at a mental health trust already subject to a statutory inquiry into at least 2,000 deaths.
